s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive visual impairment with endocrine dysfunction
salient_findings: Sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm
key_facts: 2-week history of rapidly progressive visual reduction
Vestibular schwannoma treated by gamma-knife radiosurgery 2 years earlier
Mass compressing the optic chiasm and extending toward the left cavernous sinus
Lesion predominantly isointense to gray matter on T1-weighted images
Diffuse homogeneous enhancement after contrast administration
Normal pituitary gland on MRI 2 years earlier

raw.rationale: The patient's rapidly progressive visual reduction, bitemporal hemianopsia, and a 2-cm sellar/suprasellar mass compressing the optic chiasm are consistent with a pituitary adenoma. The lesion's characteristics on MRI, including its isointensity to gray matter on T1-weighted images and hyperintensity on T2-weighted images with diffuse homogeneous enhancement, also support this diagnosis. Additionally, the elevated prolactin level is a common finding in pituitary adenomas.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Craniopharyngiomas are typically seen in a younger population and often have calcifications on imaging, which were not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningiomas are usually dural-based and have a different appearance on MRI, often with a dural tail sign, which was not described in the case.

rejected.label: Pituitary apoplexy
rejected.why: Pituitary apoplexy typically presents with sudden onset of severe headache, visual loss, and altered mental status, which does not match the patient's 2-week history of progressive symptoms.

rejected.label: Hypophysitis
rejected.why: Hypophysitis is an inflammatory condition of the pituitary gland, which would not typically cause a discrete mass compressing the optic chiasm as seen in this case.
